name: TutorMoments
summary: 520 moments from real one-to-one math tutoring sessions, U.S. grades 2 to 7, each cut where the tutor's next move matters and labelled by experienced teachers: the learner needs scaffolding, or a push for rigor.

license.note: CC BY 4.0, for research and educational use under Ai2's Responsible Use Guidelines. The learners are minors, de-identified (imperfectly, its card says): never try to re-identify them, or pass on a record with personal details left in. Its replays hold other models' words, under their providers' terms.
license.terms: research and educational use, under Ai2's Responsible Use Guidelines; never try to re-identify a learner

cite: Zhang, A., Ross, A., Patel, K., Bernado, J., Bowie, R., Trindade Ribeiro, A., Halper, D., Valayaputtur, H., Andreas, J., Loeb, S., Lucy, L., Lo, K., & Knight, R. (2026). When Help is Unhelpful: Evaluating AI Tutors for Productive Struggle. Hugging Face. https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/tutormoments-preview

fits.how: Each moment that ends on the learner becomes a test case (485 of the 520): the conversation up to the cut, with what the teachers said the learner needs as the rubric. It tests what a teacher's How the AI helps controls: when to help and when to hold back.

connect.note: A real learner at a moment teachers marked: does the reply scaffold where they need it and push for rigor where they can go further? Half of each. Minors' de-identified words go to your model and your judge, so use a provider whose terms allow it. Asks you to accept its terms first.
